thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Fee-based model: intact, with demonstrated resilience in Q3 [D02], [D10]
Development pipeline: intact, with 515,400 rooms in backlog [D02], [D04]
Management execution: intact, with continued focus on capital-light growth [D02], [D10]
Valuation: changed; stock trades at 37.7x FY2025 EPS guidance, significantly higher than the 23x multiple in 2019 [D05], [D10]

drivers.driver: The current valuation at nearly 38x earnings significantly compresses prospective IRRs compared to our 20% hurdle for new capital.
Persistent RevPAR weakness and macro headwinds necessitate a more conservative outlook for long-term compounding.

final.memo:
We remain admirers of the Company as a dominant, fee-generative franchise [D02], [D10]. The business model has proven its resilience, generating 8% adjusted EBITDA growth in Q3 despite a 1.1% decline in system-wide comparable RevPAR [D04], [D10]. The capital-light nature of the brand-distribution loop and the robust development pipeline remain key pillars of our thesis [D02], [D10].

However, at a share price of $301.86, the stock trades at approximately 37.7x the midpoint of 2025 adjusted EPS guidance [D05]. This valuation is a material step-up from the 23x multiple at which we initially underwrote the investment [D05], [D10]. While the franchise is excellent, we cannot ignore that the market is now fully capitalizing a long runway of growth, leaving little room for error should macroeconomic headwinds—such as tariff uncertainty or continued soft travel demand—persist [D06], [D10].

Our investment mandate is to achieve high rates of return, and at these levels, the prospective IRR is unlikely to meet our 15-20% thresholds [D10]. We are choosing to trim our position to reallocate capital toward opportunities offering more attractive asymmetric profiles. We remain disciplined in our valuation; owning a great business at any price is not the Pershing Square way [D05], [D10].
